scope: Exact local write-once intent/application-ledger workflow, separate application of the already judged Genesis 4:8 note/connected-metadata candidate, and the exact five-replacement current sample-test migration. This is not a canonical writer, source-form judgment or publication approval.

review_rationale: Fixed baseline, candidate, candidate judgment, frozen preflight, dependency manifest and all prior package pins are checked before work. Exact executor, tests, application document, migration and root-method bytes are bound to this separate transaction approval.

Historical Genesis baseline replay is explicit and narrowly targets one record. The unchanged Jeremiah and Numbers wrappers compose to reproduce the frozen whole-OT sample and 101 contexts; unrelated corpus drift still fails. Actual corpus digest and complete GEN export are computed outside all overlays.

A candidate state or existing intent requires the prepared intent and matching review. Applied receipts bind the exact intent bytes and status. Existing application plus restored baseline is rejected as unrecorded rollback. Ledger creation is exclusive/write-once, and prepare, complete and post_check check relevant byte stability.

The migration recognizes only its exact baseline or candidate current-test bytes. Its explicit Path.read_bytes argument avoids the older default-reader capture bypassing composed historical views. Frozen checks and artifacts are not edited.

The frozen nine Genesis candidate tests use frozen fixtures and validate_records, not the current-canonical run function. They may remain in the full regression suite unchanged; no exclusion or invented post-application test failure is justified. The frozen checker run is replayed historically, separately from the live full-GEN check.

Pinned historical dossiers and derivative contexts remain historical. Seventeen unchanged simplified/multilingual records are not synchronized by this application, and Hebrew-source equality does not certify English-note freshness.

The local workflow does not claim atomic multi-file protection against arbitrary concurrent writers. The authorized operator must preserve the exact review and package, prepare first, apply the exact candidate and exact test migration separately, complete, and perform a fresh independent post-application check.
